disposition_reason: Narrative review (Agriculture 2025, 15, 433; explicitly not exhaustive) of Cd sources, uptake and mitigation in cacao. It summarises soil amendments, Zn/Mn, low-Cd genotypes and rootstocks, microbes, testa removal and blending, and cites bean Cd values from other studies (Table 1, regional averages). All mitigation outcomes are qualitative or relative (e.g. 13-fold genotype range); no new measurements. Bean values are secondary and recorded only as flagged findings.

controls.design: review (secondary summary of pot/field trials refs [56],[31],[71],[72],[73])
controls.outcome: Qualitative in review: soil pH up, topsoil Cd availability down; ref [56] (Argüello et al., seedlings) Cd uptake from subsurface increased when surface limed; ref [73] reduced Cd in leaves 'but not in beans'; ref [72] some commercial liming materials increased Cd uptake; 'field results remain inconsistent'. No numeric bean-Cd changes reported.
Lime+biochar: reduced soil Cd phytoavailability and leaf Cd (refs [68,71]); gypsum and lime+compost: reduced leaf Cd but not bean Cd (ref [73]); results 'inconsistent'. No numbers.

controls.control: Soil or foliar zinc and soil manganese application
controls.outcome: Zn decreased Cd uptake and transport to leaves in young CCN-51 plants (ref [90]); foliar Zn promotes Cd sequestration in vegetative tissue, reducing allocation to beans (ref [21]); Mn induced detoxification proteins (ref [91]). No numeric bean-Cd outcomes.

controls.control: Low-Cd phosphate fertilizers / limiting Cd inputs from phosphate rock
controls.outcome: Recommended as 'critical' given cacao on acidic, Cd-rich, long-fertilized soils; no measured effect reported.

controls.control: Selection of low-Cd genotypes (e.g. IMC-67, ICS-1 low; NA-312, SCA-5 high)
controls.design: review (secondary; ref [104] Lewis et al., 100 cultivars, International Cocoa Genebank Trinidad, uniform soil)
controls.comparator: other accessions grown under uniform soil conditions
controls.outcome: Bean Cd varied 13-fold and leaf Cd 7-fold among 100 cultivars (ref [104]); 11 of 53 Peruvian genotypes incl. TSH-565 and CCN-51 had lower Cd (ref [105]). Review cautions TSH-565, ICS-1, CCN-51 and PS13-19 were low accumulators under some conditions and high under others. No absolute bean values given.

CCN-51/BN-34 and CCN-51/PH-16 retained more Cd in roots, reducing leaf and bean Cd under soil Cd up to 150 mg/kg (cited as ref [112]); ICS-95 on IMC-67 rootstock accumulated less Cd than CCN-51 on the same rootstock (ref [113]). No numeric bean values.

controls.control: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi / Cd-tolerant fungi and bacteria (bioremediation)
controls.outcome: Native AMF decreased Cd uptake by IMC-67 (ref [116]); AMF spores plus organic amendments reduced Cd in plant tissues (ref [117]); Talaromyces santanderensis tolerance index 0.81 at 300 mg/kg Cd. Described as early-stage; no bean-Cd numbers.

controls.control: Removal of bean testa (seed coat) for genotypes that store Cd in the testa
controls.design: review (suggestion citing ref [104]; mechanism from ref [17])
controls.outcome: Seed coat Cd up to 1.8x the seed during development, but 91% of Cd remobilized into the seed before maturity, leaving 9% in the seed coat before fermentation (ref [17]); so shell removal is suggested only for specific genotypes. No measured post-harvest reduction.

controls.control: Blending beans from low- and high-Cd regions
controls.outcome: Proposed to lower overall Cd in cocoa products; no numbers.

controls.design: review (citing refs [10],[17],[20] - Meter et al. 2019, CBI)
controls.outcome: Unofficial industry guideline for beans 0.50-1.10 mg/kg DW; suggested maximum safe levels 0.6 and 0.8 mg/kg FW for peeled beans; some buyers reject beans above 0.1 or 0.3 mg/kg. 53% of Ecuadorian bean samples from six provinces exceeded 0.80 mg/kg DW (ref [27] Barraza).

regulatory.product: chocolate and cocoa powder, 'depending on the cacao content of the product'
regulatory.status: cited range 0.10 to 0.80 mg Cd/kg; in force since 2019
regulatory.integrity_issue: Review states the limits are 'mg Cd kg−1 dry matter'; EU 488/2014 cocoa/chocolate limits are expressed on the product as sold, not dry matter. Use the regulation text, not this review, for values.

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary writes 'South and Central America 1.39 mg/kg DW (average)'; primary gives South America 1.39 and Central America 0.54 mg/kg separately, with no basis stated.
Stored summary labels the Table 1 bean column and regional averages 'mg/kg DW'; Table 1 and the regional-average sentence do not state a basis.
Stored Table 1 omits the Peru [21] row (0.17 ± 0.41 and 1.78 ± 0.35 µg/g) and the Ecuador [40] subsurface soil range (0.06-2.59), and adds a 'Brazil' row not present in the primary.
Stored summary calls it a 'Systematic review'; primary says it 'does not aim to cover all aspects of Cd in cacao exhaustively' (narrative review).
Stored summary repeats the review's EU 'dry matter' basis for 488/2014 without flagging it.
unresolved: Meaning of paired values printed with 'and' in Table 1 (Costa Rica [36], [49]; Ecuador [31]; Peru [21]) is not explained; originals needed.

Text attributes the CCN-51/BN-34 and CCN-51/PH-16 rootstock result to ref [112], but Table 2 assigns rootstock combinations to refs [113] and [114] and ref [112] to leaf proteome; citation mapping inconsistent.
Genotype named 'THS-565' in one sentence and 'TSH-565' in another; presumably TSH-565.
Seed coat 1.8x and 91% remobilisation figures attributed to ref [17] (Vanderschueren 2021), itself a review; original measurement not identified.
